paper_000.pdf: Floquet treatment of driven graphene predicts photon-dressed Dirac states and light-induced modifications near the Dirac cone.
Circular polarization can open gaps and produce Hall-like responses via Floquet-engineered Berry curvature.
paper_001.pdf: tr-ARPES can directly observe Floquet-Bloch sidebands as energy-spaced replicas of a Dirac cone.
Avoided crossings and polarization dependence are central observables under mid-infrared pumping.
paper_002.pdf: Floquet engineering modifies topological band structure on ultrafast timescales; repeated quasienergy-zone picture is relevant for driven Dirac materials.
paper_003.pdf: Theory for graphene pump-probe photoemission predicts Floquet band formation from realistic short pulses.
Graphene-specific interpretation should focus on replica bands, local gap/crossing behavior, and pseudospin-related modifications rather than overclaiming topological phase realization.

impact_on_contract: Use tr-ARPES-style energy-momentum maps as main evidence figures.
Quantify replica energy spacing relative to the drive photon energy.
Discuss polarization dependence conservatively because provided data emphasize linear-polarization modulation more than circular-gap opening.
